plan_a_advantages: More targeted speed development with intervals and tempo runs.
Includes strength training to support trail running demands.
Greater variety of session types to mimic race conditions.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses heavily on building a strong aerobic base.
Longer long runs, potentially beneficial for ultra-distance preparation (though not the primary goal).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more strategic blend of intensity and volume, directly addressing the need for speed development through interval training and tempo runs. Plan B, while emphasizing endurance, lacks sufficient structured speed work, which is crucial for improving pace on trails. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training also supports the demands of trail running, while Plan B’s hill sessions are less focused on overall speed gains.  Furthermore, the variety of session types in Plan A – intervals, tempo, cross-training – better mimics the varied demands of a trail race compared to Plan B’s more repetitive long runs.
